evals.prompt: We just finished docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md for our Kedata project and §3 locks us into a single VM running Docker Compose (one app service plus a worker). Can you turn that into the actual deploy setup — Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, the CI/CD pipeline, and a DEPLOYMENT.md runbook we can hand to ops?
evals.expected_output: A complete VM + Docker Compose deployment surface for the app service and worker: a Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml matching the runtime, port, and env matrix from the plan and ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md, a CI/CD pipeline that builds and gates on the test suites before deploying on push to main, and a DEPLOYMENT.md runbook covering build, secrets handling, database migrations with backup, health checks, rollout, and rollback — all consistent with the platform already chosen in plan §3.
assertions: The agent's response contains a Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml defining both the app service and the worker, with the port and environment variables taken from the plan and env matrix rather than invented.
The agent produced a DEPLOYMENT.md runbook that includes build steps, secrets handling, migration/backup procedure, health checks, rollout, and a concrete rollback path.

The agent's CI/CD configuration triggers on push to main and runs the deploy-gating test suites before deploying, without proposing a different platform than the VM + Docker Compose decision in plan §3.

evals.prompt: Our plan §3 locks us into a single VM with Docker Compose. I want two compose files: one that brings up the whole stack (app plus Postgres and Redis), and one that runs only the app against our shared dev Postgres and Redis. Host ports must be configurable so they do not clash on anyone's machine, and the DB/cache endpoints must come from env.
evals.expected_output: Two compose files: docker-compose.yml as the full stack (app plus Postgres/Redis with volumes and healthchecks) and docker-compose.dev.yml with only the application service(s), reaching the DB/cache through env vars. Every published host port is env-parameterized with a default (for example ${APP_HOST_PORT:-8080}), and the third-party endpoints/credentials are supplied via env and listed in .env.example, not hard-coded.
assertions: The response defines docker-compose.yml as the full stack (app plus the database and cache) and docker-compose.dev.yml with only the application service(s).
Every published host port uses env interpolation with a default (for example ${APP_HOST_PORT:-8080} and ${DB_HOST_PORT:-5432}), so host ports are configurable and do not clash.
Database and cache connection details come from environment variables (with defaults or required markers) in both files, and are not hard-coded.
